title: Cohere Chases $5B Round as Canada Buys a Stake
dek: Ottawa backs Cohere's push to build frontier AI outside the U.S. and China.

facts.label: Maximum size of Cohere's Series E
Valuation if the full round closes

caption:
A national government just bought into an AI lab. 🇨🇦

Cohere has closed the first part of a Series E that could reach CAD $7 billion, about US $5 billion. That would value the Toronto company at CAD $35.7 billion. Schwarz Group leads the round, Nvidia is back, and the Government of Canada is committing up to CAD $1.6 billion in stages. Prime Minister Mark Carney called it a matter of national security.

Cohere is pitching sovereign AI: models that democratic countries and companies can inspect, host and control themselves. The money will fund new models, the Aleph Alpha combination, the AISLE deal and a new Cohere Cyber product for classified, air-gapped settings.

We're tracking the sovereign AI race daily at AI Parabellum. Can Cohere really compete with OpenAI and the Chinese labs?

post_caption:
Canada isn't waiting for the U.S. or China to decide its AI future.

Ottawa is taking an equity stake in Cohere as part of a record Series E worth up to CAD $7 billion, backed by Schwarz Group and Nvidia. Cohere says ARR grew 165% and its customer count hit 300, with Bell, RBC and TD Bank among them.
